key_insight: Neural surrogates trained on quantum-hardware QAOA samples accelerated autocorrelation decay in constrained Boltzmann sampling beyond 1,000 binary variables.
engineering_relevance: Divide-and-conquer sampling offers a route to larger constrained systems without requiring a quantum processor to represent the full problem at once.
method: Generate QAOA training samples using an IBM Quantum Heron r2 processor.
Train neural surrogates to support quantum-enhanced MCMC sampling.
Use a divide-and-conquer strategy to handle larger systems.
evidence_signal: Tests covered N=144 and N=1064 variables; at N=1064, autocorrelation decay per MCMC step was approximately 5.2× and 12.3× that of global and local Kawasaki dynamics, respectively.
watch_item: Larger subproblem blocks challenged neural-surrogate learning, and faster decay per MCMC step does not establish end-to-end runtime advantage.
paper_title: Hardware Demonstration of Neural-Surrogated Quantum-Enhanced MCMC for Large-Scale Constrained Boltzmann Sampling
